# Form Studio 0.40 — release acceptance

This is an acceptance protocol, not a completed certification. Record the exact
build hash, Mac model/RAM/macOS, tester, date, result and evidence for each run.
Use disposable copies of projects. Never test interruption against a customer's
only copy. Do not run the launch smoke script during manual desktop testing: it
owns and terminates a separate application instance.

## Intended first release

Apple Silicon macOS desktop **private beta**, centred on local sketch → exact
solid → editable creative mesh → material → save/reopen/export workflows.
Support Intel, Windows or Linux only after separate qualification; the current
arm64 DMG is not universal. The browser companion is not proof of desktop
native-engine correctness, and headless React tests do not verify WebView/GPU UI.

Garment fitting/physical calibration, engineering analysis, specialist BIM,
advanced rigging and GPU rendering require workflow-specific acceptance. Expose
limitations in the UI and release notes. A numerical fit score is not measured
fit, a beam estimate is not validated FEA, and an interchange fixture passing is
not universal compatibility. Licensed DWG and third-party approvals cannot be
promised without the relevant licenses and evidence.

## Automated candidate checks

Run `npm run release:certify` on a quiet, supported Mac. The runner records each
check and its log under `release-evidence/runs/`, checkpoints progress, bounds test
process concurrency and terminates a timed-out check's process group. Failed or
interrupted checks do not become a passing certification. Keep performance
budgets unchanged; profile repeatable failures rather than granting exceptions
because the host was busy.

The local ad-hoc signature check only validates package structure/integrity. A
passing local candidate must still report public distribution as unapproved.

## Manual desktop gates

| Gate | Procedure | Required outcome |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Save cancellation | Edit, Save As, cancel, continue editing | No lost changes; dirty state remains; next save works |
| Save round trip | Save a named file, edit and save again, reopen | Same dimensions, materials, graph/animation/texture content; backup contains previous revision |
| Unsaved close/quit | Edit; test window close and Cmd-Q separately; choose Keep editing | App remains open with edits intact |
| Saved quit | Save, wait for completion, quit/relaunch/open | No false dirty prompt; saved data intact |
| Recovery | In a disposable document, allow autosave; terminate that test instance; relaunch and recover | Latest valid checkpoint loads; invalid/partial checkpoint does not replace saved file |
| Failure during write | Disposable project with inaccessible backup/output path | Clear error; old project still readable; retry to a writable destination succeeds |
| Workspace transitions | CAD → Fabric → CAD and CAD → Rig → CAD | Document identity, filename, edits and workspace data preserved |
| History | Modify geometry, nodes, animation, bake and paint; Undo/Redo; branch after Undo | Correct state restored; no old document after Open; one paint/curve drag per entry |
| Interrupted gestures | Paint/curve drag; Escape, pointer cancel, lost capture, blur | Preview cancelled, controls released, committed content unchanged |
| Five representative projects | Bracket; patterned creative object; garment; animated assembly; multi-storey BIM | Save/reopen/edit/export complete without unexpected errors; specialist limitations documented |
| External interchange | Reopen exports in independent recipient applications | Units, bounds, topology and intended semantics checked, not just file existence |
| Long session | Two hours alternating edit/save/undo/import/render on dense fixtures | No progressive input stalls, unexplained memory growth or lost work; capture peak RSS/frame times |
| Constrained layout | Small supported window, dense inspector, keyboard-only flow | Save/Open/Undo/Cancel reachable; no trapped scrolling, hidden blocking dialogs or clipped critical controls |

## Owner-controlled public distribution gates

- Supply a staffed public support address and a separate private security contact.
  Define response ownership, disclosure handling, incident/key-rotation procedure
  and known-issues page. Do not invent addresses or expose private vulnerabilities.
- Configure Developer ID and notarization credentials in the release secret
  store, not source or chat; configure the updater public trust root and keep its
  signing key private. Follow `docs/MACOS_RELEASE.md`.
- Build from a reviewed, clean release commit; verify the exact app and DMG's
  Developer ID signature, Gatekeeper assessment, notarization staple and updater
  signature. A prior artifact's signature does not validate a rebuilt binary.
- Install on a clean Mac without development dependencies. Test first launch,
  permissions, offline operation, upgrade and rollback with project backups.
- Obtain external artist/manufacturing acceptance for advertised workflows.
  Physical cloth qualification needs measured specimens and independent
  correlation. Until then, label fit/simulation as experimental rather than
  treating synthetic samples as laboratory evidence.
- Require an explicit owner go/no-go before public publishing. A green local
  test report alone must never trigger public release.

## Bug report minimum

Build hash/version; hardware/macOS; exact steps; expected/actual result; disposable
reproducer if permitted; screenshot; relevant diagnostics; whether save/recovery
worked. Review exported diagnostics for sensitive paths/project information before
sharing. Attach no customer assets, credentials or private signing material.
